headline: Graph neural networks extend to molecular, antibody, and protein interaction prediction
label: Graph Learning For Biomolecular Prediction
summary: Recent preprints apply graph neural networks and attention to ligand, antibody, and interaction-network prediction, with one published molecular study.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learning on graph representations of molecular and biomolecular data, with graph encoders combined with complementary information. XIMP couples molecular graphs with junction-tree and pharmacophore abstractions through cross-graph message passing. GPCR-Filter fuses ESM-3 receptor embeddings with graph neural network ligand encodings via attention, and RAG-GNN combines graph embeddings with retrieved literature knowledge through gated fusion and contrastive alignment. PCEvo instead derives molecular representations from virtual chemical edit paths between similar molecules under a path-consistency objective. Multispecific antibody function is predicted from domain topology, DMG-PPI models similarity and complementarity in protein-protein interaction networks, and TurboGAE applies subgraph-level tokenization with multimodal fusion to molecular property prediction. The新 element across these items is multi-source or multi-view abstraction layered on graph encoders rather than graph structure alone. Most items are preprints; TurboGAE is the only published entry.
